candidates.exact_span: Select only those Elements and Sections which apply to your sludge reuse or disposal practice.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Elements and Sections are selected determines which sludge monitoring and reporting requirements are applicable for FY2025, and whether missing or absent DMR data reflects non-applicable requirements versus unresolved obligations.

candidates.exact_span: If your facility utilizes more than one type of disposal or reuse method (for example, Element I and Element II apply) or the quality of your sludge varies (for example, Section II and Section III of Element I apply) use a separate Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) for each Section that is applicable.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether multiple disposal methods or sludge-quality categories apply requires separate DMRs per Section; a different interpretation of facility practice changes which monitoring obligations exist and how missing evidence on a single DMR should be read.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge DMRs shall be due by February 19th of each year and shall cover the previous January through December time period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The January–December reporting period and February 19 due date define which calendar months fall within each sludge DMR cycle; interpreting how that cycle maps to Federal FY2025 (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30) changes whether monitoring was required and whether reported or missing data pertains to the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: (The sludge DMRs for permits in Texas shall be due by September 1 of each year, with the reporting period of August 1 to July 31)
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this permit is treated as Texas-subject, the August 1–July 31 reporting period and September 1 due date replace the default schedule, altering which FY2025 months are covered by required sludge DMRs and how absent reports are classified.

candidates.exact_span: The sludge conditions do not apply to wastewater treatment lagoons where sludge is not wasted for final reuse/disposal.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a lagoon facility wastes sludge for final reuse/disposal determines whether Part IV sludge limits, monitoring obligations, and DMR expectations apply at all for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: If the sludge is not removed, the permittee shall indicate on the DMR "No Discharge".
candidates.computation_change_reason: When sludge is not removed, the required "No Discharge" DMR notation is the operative evidence for a documented no-discharge/no-removal state versus required monitoring that lacks adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Page 6 - Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge for Application to the Land Meeting Class A or B Pathogen Reduction and the Cumulative Loading Rates in Table 2, or Class B Pathogen Reduction and the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of Element 1 Section II hinges on pathogen class and whether compliance is measured against Table 2 cumulative loading rates or Table 3 pollutant concentrations, which selects different enforceable numeric limit sets and associated monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Page 10 - Requirements Specific to Bulk Sewage Sludge Meeting Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3 and Class A Pathogen Reduction Requirements
candidates.computation_change_reason: Element 1 Section III applies only when sludge meets Table 3 pollutant concentrations and Class A pathogen reduction; interpreting sludge quality against those criteria changes which numeric limits and monitoring requirements govern bulk land application.

candidates.exact_span: Page 12 - Requirements Specific to Sludge Sold or Given Away in a Bag or Other Container for Application to the Land that does not meet the Pollutant Concentrations in Table 3
candidates.computation_change_reason: Element 1 Section IV applies to bagged or containerized sludge that fails Table 3 pollutant concentrations; whether sludge is sold/given away in that form and whether it meets Table 3 determines a distinct limit and monitoring regime.

candidates.exact_span: Page 19 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites Without a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Element 2 Section II versus Section III splits surface-disposal obligations by liner and leachate-collection presence; the site configuration interpretation selects different enforceable limits and monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: Page 20 - Requirements Specific to Surface Disposal Sites With a Liner and Leachate Collection System
candidates.computation_change_reason: Element 2 Section III applies only where a liner and leachate collection system are present; interpreting site design determines whether these alternate numeric limits and monitoring duties replace the Section II requirements.
